key_insight: An optimized gradient boosting decision tree predicted friction stir-welded 7N01 aluminum joint strength with R² = 0.978 and mapped welding process windows targeting at least 90% joint efficiency.
engineering_relevance: The approach provides a quantitative basis for selecting welding parameters, with shoulder plunge depth helping refine the high-strength process window.
method: Predict ultimate tensile strength from rotational speed, welding speed, and shoulder plunge depth.
Compare baseline models, then optimize gradient boosting hyperparameters using grid search.
Use SHAP to interpret parameter effects and map predicted high-strength process windows.
evidence_signal: Using 27 experimental samples and leave-one-out cross-validation, reported R² increased from 0.905 for the decision tree baseline to 0.966 for gradient boosting and 0.978 after tuning.
watch_item: The small dataset and absence of reported independent validation warrant experimental confirmation of the predicted process windows before deployment.
paper_title: Interpretable ensemble learning for tensile strength prediction and welding process window optimization of friction stir-welded 7N01 aluminum alloy
